subsystems.name: Ultramafic rock reservoir
subsystems.role: the reactor: iron-rich olivine and pyroxene that water attacks, releasing hydrogen.

subsystems.name: Fluid circulation
subsystems.role: moves water through the hot rock and carries dissolved gases back out.

subsystems.name: Reaction products
subsystems.role: what serpentinisation makes: serpentine, magnetite, brucite, hydrogen, methane and heat.
parts: hydrogen and methane in the effluent

subsystems.name: Surface plant and gas handling
subsystems.role: separates and purifies hydrogen from a wet, gas-rich fluid stream.

subsystems.name: Monitoring network
subsystems.role: tracks how fast the rock reacts and whether the plumbing is clogging.

subsystems.name: Laboratory and modelling chain
subsystems.role: turns field samples into a reaction network that can be predicted and scaled.

subsystems.name: Ocean-world analogue instruments
subsystems.role: payloads that look for the same chemistry far from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Find the rock
buildSteps.detail: Target iron-rich ultramafic rock near the surface: ophiolite belts on land, or exposed mantle on the seafloor such as the Atlantis Massif.

buildSteps.title: Characterise it
buildSteps.detail: Drill and core the rock to measure olivine content, fracture density and permeability — the properties that set how much hydrogen a volume of rock can yield.

buildSteps.title: Complete the wells
buildSteps.detail: Adapt geothermal drilling to create injection and production wells with sealed intervals, so water can be pushed through rock rather than short-circuiting to the surface.

buildSteps.title: Stimulate the reaction
buildSteps.detail: Inject warm water, and sometimes carbon dioxide, to open fresh fracture surface. Serpentinisation is fastest and most hydrogen-rich around 200–300 °C.

buildSteps.title: Circulate and let the rock react
buildSteps.detail: Water oxidises iron in the olivine, forming serpentine, magnetite and brucite while releasing hydrogen and heat. Efficiency depends on how long fluid stays in contact.

buildSteps.title: Recover the gas
buildSteps.detail: Bring the effluent to the surface, separate hydrogen and methane from water and carbon dioxide, and purify to fuel-cell or industrial grade.

buildSteps.title: Watch for clogging
buildSteps.detail: Serpentine and brucite swell and fill pore space, so permeability falls over time; monitoring decides when to refracture or move to new rock.

buildSteps.title: Replicate in the lab
buildSteps.detail: Run crushed rock in high-pressure reactors at controlled temperature and fluid chemistry to measure kinetics and test whether added catalysts raise hydrogen yields.

buildSteps.title: Carry the question to ocean worlds
buildSteps.detail: Fly mass spectrometers and sample-handling instruments to Enceladus and Europa to detect hydrogen, methane and organics that would indicate the same reaction running under an ice shell.

prerequisites.why: the fluid must be delivered to and recovered from hot rock hundreds of metres down, using methods borrowed from geothermal and oil practice.
hydrogen and methane can come from microbes or from rock; carbon and hydrogen isotopes are needed to tell them apart.
the chemistry is well described, but predicting rates and yields in a real fracture network is still uncertain.
the reaction that makes the hydrogen also seals the flow paths, and no field method has yet sustained output over years.
hydrogen embrittles steel and leaks readily, so well materials and surface separation must be adapted.
spectrometers are built and flying, but reaching a subsurface ocean and returning a clean sample remains unsolved.

pathway.milestone: year-round study of active serpentinising systems — the Lost City field on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, sampled since its discovery in 2000, and scientific drilling in the Samail Ophiolite in Oman
pathway.unlocks: a measured reaction network and evidence that rock–water chemistry alone can feed a microbial ecosystem.

pathway.milestone: paired field and laboratory experiments that pin down hydrogen yields, reaction rates and the role of catalysts over long timescales
pathway.unlocks: credible estimates of how much natural hydrogen a given rock volume could deliver.

pathway.milestone: in-situ stimulation pilots adapted from enhanced geothermal practice, with tracers to confirm the gas is abiotic and newly made
pathway.unlocks: the first real test of whether engineered serpentinisation can be an energy source rather than a curiosity.

pathway.milestone: Cassini found molecular hydrogen in the plume of Enceladus; Europa Clipper, launched in 2024, will survey Europa's ice and chemistry from orbit
pathway.unlocks: a way to judge whether alkaline serpentinising chemistry is common on ocean worlds.

pathway.milestone: either natural hydrogen becomes a niche low-carbon fuel, or the programme settles the question of whether this chemistry is a plausible cradle for life
pathway.unlocks: a resource answer and a origins-of-life answer, in either case on a firm measured footing.
